correctness.rationale: The length-zero equations a_i²=0 eliminate the idempotent coordinates on reduction. The remaining equations are b_i b_{i+1}=0 and b_i c_{i+1}+c_i b_{i+2}=0, with the length-three coordinates free. On an independent support, gaps of length 2, 3, and at least 4 give ranks 1, 1, and 2 respectively, on disjoint sets of c-coordinates. Solving with invertible torus coordinates proves the claimed product isomorphisms in any characteristic, including the empty-support affine space. The strata are geometrically irreducible. In a finite union of their closures, every irreducible component is one of those closures; the full-dimensional closures are distinct by their coordinate supports and are exactly the empty support and the maximal independent supports. The class and point formulas follow by additivity. Marking a support vertex gives the n/r factor even for periodic gap lists; summing the weights and taking a formal logarithmic derivative proves the normalized series. As a bounded independent check, enumerate masks with no cyclically adjacent bits for n=4 through 8, set b to the mask, and row-reduce the displayed c-equations over F2. Each rank was r+h; the independent totals from summing 2^(2n−rank) were 640, 3584, 17408, 88064, 450560. This supports the binary instances only; the all-field proof is algebraic. The supplied verifier was inspected, not run; no expert or formal attestation is asserted.

evidence: The mirror proves every nontrivial row/column incidence component is a star with at most two edges. Every edge coefficient is a unit on the support torus.
The mirror expressly does not state an irreducible-component theorem.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For each star choose a fixed unit pivot. A one-row star eliminates one variable by a Laurent-polynomial substitution; for a one-column star it sets that variable to zero and the other row is redundant. This gives exactly the trivial product claimed in the frozen record. Additivity, maximal-dimensional closure of strata, and the known count of maximal supports then give the motivic class and top-component theorem as direct consequences, even though not explicitly stated there. This logical implication does not determine historical priority.

originality.rationale: The full frozen claim is not established as distinct from existing coverage. The strongest distinct Resultary record has precisely the same equations and support-dependent ranks, not just the same counts. Although it does not state the geometric theorems, its disjoint-star proof directly yields the supportwise trivializations. The geometric conclusions then follow by finite stratification, the standard dimension argument and the known Perrin count. Its catalogue date is later, so this is a finding of equivalent coverage, not a finding of earlier priority or derivation by either author from the other.
residual_risks: Relative historical priority and the relationship between the two records are not established; the comparison establishes logical coverage.
